success_patterns: Interpret limit-superior and limit-inferior claims literally, especially at infinite endpoints: a limsup of minus infinity forces eventual divergence below every finite threshold, whereas a liminf of minus infinity can express only arbitrarily late subsequential dips.

Compare algorithmic guarantees by both their output and their behavior on negative instances: producing a witness when one exists does not necessarily decide that none exists, and a yes/no decision procedure need not produce a witness.
Keep subgroup rank distinct from ambient rank and free-factor rank; the rank of a subgroup can exceed the rank of its ambient free group, while a free factor cannot.

patch.reasoning: The skill already captures exact theorem matching, quantifier auditing, extra-clause verification, and the distinction between subgroup rank and free-factor rank. Two useful refinements from this batch are the precise semantics of limsup versus liminf at minus infinity and the difference between witness-producing and decision algorithms.

edits.target: - Preserve the exact form of asymptotic assertions: note cutoffs, the order of iterated limits, and whether the claim uses a limit or limsup. Do not silently replace a truncated approximation with convergence to a full series.
edits.content: - At an infinite endpoint, distinguish the meanings of limsup and liminf: limsup of a quantity equal to minus infinity means it is eventually below every finite threshold, while liminf equal to minus infinity may only guarantee arbitrarily late subsequential dips. Do not treat these as equivalent unless existence of the full limit is established.

edits.target: - For algorithm bounds, distinguish a fixed-parameter form f(k)n^c from n^{O(k)}: polynomial time for each fixed k alone does not establish FPT.
edits.content: - Distinguish a witness-producing promise from a decision procedure. An algorithm guaranteed to produce a witness when one exists need not terminate or answer no when none exists; a yes/no decider, in turn, need not output a witness.
